title: Force
subject: Physics

English.simple_explanation: A force is a push or pull on an object.
English.detailed_explanation: A net force can change an object's motion by speeding it up, slowing it down, changing its direction, or changing its shape.
English.everyday_example: Pushing a door open and pulling a drawer closed are both examples of force.

local_example.text: Pulling a fishing net is an everyday example of applying a force.
local_example.appropriate_usage: Use as a local-context draft only until reviewed by a community or content reviewer.

common_misconceptions: A moving object always needs a continuing push to keep moving.

observe_around_you.invitation: Find something heavy you can push on the floor — a full bucket, a sack, a wooden box.
observe_around_you.what_to_do: Push it gently until it just starts to move. Then push it much harder and watch how quickly it picks up speed.
observe_around_you.what_to_notice: There is a push small enough that nothing happens at all. Find that point. Then notice that a harder push does not just move it — it moves it sooner.
observe_around_you.concept_link: A force is a push or a pull that can change motion. Below a certain push, friction cancels you out entirely. Above it, more force gives more acceleration, not more speed by itself.
observe_around_you.safety_note: Push, do not pull towards yourself, and keep your feet clear of the load.

think_question: Can an object move without a force continuously pushing it? What forces might slow it down?

misconception_keywords: force is needed to keep moving
reasoning_guide.correct_feedback: Good reasoning: you connected forces such as friction to changes in motion.
reasoning_guide.partial_feedback: Explain which force can slow the object and how it affects motion.
reasoning_guide.misconception_feedback: A continuing push is not always needed to keep an object moving. Think about friction and other forces that change motion.

challenge.question: List three pushes or pulls you used today and name the object affected.
challenge.hint: Think about doors, bags, bicycles, or games.
progressive_hints: Think about doors, bags, bicycles, or games.
For each example, name whether you pushed or pulled and what object moved.
Use a complete sentence for at least one example.
challenge.solution: Answers differ. Examples include pushing a door, pulling a bag, or kicking a ball.

quiz_questions.question: Which statement best describes a force?
quiz_questions.explanation: A force is a push or pull acting on an object.
progressive_hints: Opening a door involves a push or a pull, not a colour or kind of energy.
